quizzes.stem: A team commits `.mcp.json` with the header `Bearer ${NPM_TOKEN}` for a hosted package registry. Every developer exports the variable, yet the registry answers 401. What is the cause?

options.a: The file loads only after an interactive approval that the developers skipped
options.b: Header values are expanded only for entries that start a local process
options.c: Claude Code reads names of this kind, which carry sign-in secrets, as empty
options.d: A variable in a header needs a fallback after the colon and dash before use

explanation.c: Credential names such as this one read as empty toward a remote endpoint.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a server that waits for approval is not connected at all: "claude mcp list shows it as pending", and it does not answer with a 401.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the documentation lists the places where expansion applies: `headers` ("for HTTP server authentication").
explanation.d: Ruled out because a default is optional, and the plain form works: "expands to the value of environment variable".

quizzes.stem: A developer needs an integration that signs in with a personal account's token. It should exist in this repository only, and the token must never reach teammates through version control. Given the three options the current product offers, where should it be registered?

options.a: Local scope, the default for a newly added server
options.b: Project scope, kept in the shared `.mcp.json` file
options.c: User scope, which loads it in all your other projects too
options.d: The local settings file, kept inside the repository

explanation.a: Local scope is the default and belongs to its owner and that one project. The guide names user-level scope for personal servers, and the product has a third scope between the two, which is the one that fits a single repository.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Selecting the wrong scope for a personal tool can leak credentials into a shared repo".
explanation.c: Ruled out because user scope is for "services you frequently use across different projects", which is wider than this repository.
explanation.d: Ruled out because that file holds settings and not servers: "while the general local settings file is `.claude/settings.local.json` in the project".

quizzes.stem: An agent keeps answering questions about the team's runbooks with Grep over a stale copy in the checkout, although an operations server has a search tool whose description reads `Searches runbooks`. What is the best fix?

options.a: Make the operations server load at the start of each session
options.b: Open its text with when to prefer it over pattern matching
options.c: Remove the competing tool from the agent's list of tools
options.d: Lengthen the text until it covers every detail of the tool

explanation.b: The description is what the model chooses by, so it must say when to prefer the tool, with the point first and the boundary against the competing tool near the start.
explanation.a: Ruled out because loading at the start only makes the definition visible: "makes the definition visible and does not say when to prefer it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Removing Grep is a blunt answer, because the agent then cannot search the code in the checkout".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Claude Code truncates each tool description and each server's instructions at 2,048 characters by default".

quizzes.stem: A support agent calls three listing tools before each answer, only to learn what the documentation site contains. Which change cuts those calls?

options.a: Expose the page tree as a resource mentioned in the prompt
options.b: Raise the output limit on the listing tools to return more entries
options.c: Mark the listing tools read-only and let them run side by side
options.d: Move the docs server into the user scope to load everywhere

explanation.a: A catalog is wanted before work starts, and a resource can be attached to the prompt so that no discovery calls are needed.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The limit concerns the size of one result and does nothing for the number of calls".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a hint "does not change this: it describes the tool to a client and does not tell the model what exists".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "it decides where a server loads and not what it exposes".

quizzes.stem: A team gives the agent its whole orders database through one MCP tool that runs any SQL it is given, and the job is to report on open orders. What is the architectural concern?

options.a: A large result set overflows, with the excess rows silently dropped
options.b: A failed list refresh drops the tool, with the job left without data
options.c: Access stays all-or-nothing, with no permission rule to scope it
options.d: Tool search withholds the definition, with the tool unusable by Claude

explanation.c: A permission rule can allow or deny a tool by name, so one tool that does everything leaves nothing to scope.
explanation.a: Ruled out because an oversized result is kept: "Claude Code saves it to a file and replaces it in the conversation with a message that names the file path".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a refresh that fails takes nothing away: "a failed refresh keeps the previous list".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a withheld definition is still brought in on demand: "a definition is loaded when Claude needs it".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools and several MCP servers. A team's shared `.mcp.json` starts a documentation server with the argument `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/tools/docs_server.py`, and on every machine the server fails to start with that text unexpanded in the path. What should the entry say?

options.a: The name moved into the `env` map so that the process receives it
options.b: An absolute location from the lead developer's own checkout, fixed for all
options.c: The same line placed in the user-level file, where the name is set
options.d: A fallback after the name, written with a colon and a dash

explanation.d: The variable is set for the server and not for Claude Code, so a path in `command` or `args` needs a fallback.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the text in `args` would still have nothing to expand from: "so `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in a project file has nothing to expand from".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a personal location fails on every other machine: "A value that is not secret, such as a base URL or a path, should have a default".
explanation.c: Ruled out because no file gives the variable a value for Claude Code, which sets it only "in the spawned server's environment to the project root".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools and several MCP servers. A CI job runs `claude -p` on a fresh clone, and a pull request has added a server to `.mcp.json` that nobody on the team has seen. What happens when the job starts?

options.a: It stays pending until a person approves it in an interactive session
options.b: It is kept out, as unreviewed servers go to `disabledMcpjsonServers`
options.c: It connects with no prompt, and Claude is given what it offers
options.d: It loads only if the repository's own settings file approves it in advance

explanation.c: Unattended runs cannot show the approval prompt.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the prompt needs a person: "In `claude -p` runs, Agent SDK sessions, and cloud sessions, Claude Code can't show that prompt: it loads project-scoped servers without asking."
explanation.b: Ruled out because that list holds only what someone writes into it: "To keep a server out anyway, list it in `disabledMcpjsonServers`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "approvals committed to the project's `.claude/settings.json` are ignored in a folder you have not trusted".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent's backend tools come from twelve MCP servers listed in the shared file. A developer reads that tools from all servers are available simultaneously and marks all twelve servers `alwaysLoad`. What is the effect?

options.a: Startup waits without limit for the servers to connect
options.b: All their definitions return to the prompt at launch, undoing deferral
options.c: Only the tools that the first request needs are loaded, the rest later
options.d: Their tool lists are fixed at launch and no longer refresh

explanation.b: `alwaysLoad` brings every definition into the initial context.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the wait is bounded: "capped at the standard 5-second connect timeout".
explanation.c: Ruled out because loading only what a request needs is what tool search does, and the flag turns that off: "Putting it on every server defeats tool search."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a connected server's list still changes: "Servers can change their tool lists while connected".
